description: We are CS and EE students from UET and FAST with experience in AI/ML and development. The Field Shift challenge lets us apply NASA Earth observation data to a real-world domain. We aim to explore AI and remote sensing to build an intuitive tool that turns complex datasets into reliable, actionable insights for farmers.
summary: Field Shift is a web-based decision-support tool that helps smallholder farmers in Punjab, Pakistan plan smarter crop rotations. Farmers simply input their district, soil type, irrigation source, and current crops. Behind the scenes, the app pulls 10 years of NASA POWER weather data and NASA MERRA-2 root-zone soil wetness for their exact location. It evaluates different crop rotations year by year based on soil health, water demand, climate resilience, and income, ranking the best options alongside realistic confidence ranges. For example, in Faisalabad, shifting from a traditional Rice-Wheat cycle to Mungbean-Chickpea cuts annual irrigation needs by 86% (from 1,226 mm down to 174 mm) and boosts soil health scores from 2.7 to 7.2 out of 10. A Random Forest model ($R^2 = 0.91$ on 2022–2024 data) also lets farmers test "what-if" rainfall and warming scenarios. The interface is available in both English and Urdu.
details:
Many farmers in Punjab rely on traditional, water-heavy crop rotations that deplete groundwater and degrade the soil over time. Field Shift replaces guesswork with local satellite data. Once a farmer enters their district, soil texture, water source, current crops, and personal priorities (like saving water or maximizing income), the app fetches a decade of daily rainfall and temperature records from NASA POWER alongside root-zone soil wetness from NASA MERRA-2.

Using FAO-56 water balance methods and local crop trait data, Field Shift builds a season-by-season table and scores every viable rotation across each individual year rather than relying on flat averages. This gives farmers a realistic performance range that reflects actual year-to-year weather swings. To help them plan ahead, we also trained a location-specific Random Forest model on pre-2022 data (achieving an R² of 0.91 on 2022–2024 holdout data for Faisalabad). This model powers interactive "what-if" scenarios for future droughts or temperature spikes without skewing the baseline historical scores.

Impact & Innovation: In water-stressed hubs like Faisalabad, switching from Rice-Wheat to Mungbean-Chickpea saves roughly 1,051 mm of irrigation water per year while naturally restoring soil nitrogen. Our goal was to bridge the gap between complex Earth observation datasets and everyday farming—turning raw satellite metrics into plain-language advice accessible in Urdu.

Tech Stack: Built with Python, Streamlit, pandas, scikit-learn, and Plotly.

Limitations: Because NASA POWER and MERRA-2 operate on a ~50 km grid, they capture regional trends rather than hyper-local microclimates. Our soil inputs rely on general texture classes, and the income metric is a simplified 1–5 relative index. Field Shift is designed to guide discussions and complement—not replace—on-the-ground advice from local agronomists.

AI Disclosure: We used AI tools (Antigravity/Gemini) as coding and documentation assistants, and Claude to help structure and design our presentation slides. All agronomic logic, dataset verification, and final project decisions were created and validated by our team.
